title: ～ば～ほど — the more ～, the more ～
summary: Shows that as one thing increases, another increases along with it: “the more ～, the more ～.” The same word is repeated: first in the ば-form, then in the dictionary form + ほど. It works for verbs and adjectives.

patterns.form: 動詞ば形 ＋ 同じ動詞辞書形 ＋ ほど、～
patterns.gloss: 読めば読むほど (the more you read)

patterns.form: い形容詞 ～ければ ＋ ～い ＋ ほど
patterns.gloss: 安ければ安いほど (the cheaper it is)

body.p: Take the verb or adjective, put it in the ば-form, then repeat it in the dictionary form and add ほど. 練習すればするほど means that the degree of practice matches the degree of progress. For な-adjectives and nouns, use なら: 静かならば静かなほど.
The second half describes a change that grows along with the first, usually with なる (上手になる, 面白くなる) or a verb showing a trend (売れる). It is a natural result, not a simple one-time event.

examples.ja: 練習（れんしゅう）すればするほど上手（じょうず）になります。
examples.romaji: Renshū sureba suru hodo jōzu ni narimasu.
examples.tr: The more you practice, the better you get.

examples.ja: この本（ほん）は読（よ）めば読（よ）むほど面白（おもしろ）くなる。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa yomeba yomu hodo omoshiroku naru.
examples.tr: The more you read this book, the more interesting it becomes.

examples.ja: 値段（ねだん）は安（やす）ければ安（やす）いほど売（う）れる。
examples.romaji: Nedan wa yasukereba yasui hodo ureru.
examples.tr: The cheaper the price, the more it sells.

pitfalls: Repeat the same word. The first part is ば-form, the second part is the dictionary form + ほど.
Do not use it for one-time actions; it describes a degree that changes continuously.
